bio.summary: Grano previously served on Boulder City Council and is running again. Her campaign focuses on middle-income housing, local economic activity and trust in city spending.
bio.in_boulder: first moved to Boulder in 2002; returned in 2007

statements.text: Downtown revitalization will absolutely be one of my top priorities if elected & you can hold me to that.
statements.speaker: Jill Grano

statements.text: Boulder definitely needs a strategy to revitalize downtown and the Hill.
statements.speaker: Jill Grano
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Jill Grano

statements.text: Grano said she didn’t see the proposed DDA as the “right mechanism” for moving forward with Downtown and University Hill business district improvements.
statements.speaker: Richard Valenty reporting Jill Grano’s interview

statements.text: Knowing what I know now about how the resignation landed for the people who elected me (even though I believed at the time I was continuing to serve them), I would not make that choice the same way.
statements.speaker: Jill Grano

statements.text: To be honest, it is hard for me to identify the city’s current top three priorities.
statements.speaker: Jill Grano

statements.text: People and businesses not feeling heard is the number one thing I hear on the campaign trail.
statements.speaker: Jill Grano
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Jill Grano

statements.text: Jill Grano is running for Boulder City Council on a platform of expanding workforce and middle-income housing, rebuilding public trust in city spending and strengthening the local economy.
statements.speaker: Boulder Reporting Lab reporter

statements.text: Armed with statistics and a firm stance on vacant commercial and residential buildings, Grano aims to boost economic vitality through the development of affordable housing, “and keeping it occupied.”
statements.speaker: Peter Constas (reporting the candidate)

statements.text: Businesses need to feel confident that customers (and employees) can enjoy downtown and the Hill safely, and that the city will respond (reliably) to open drug use and other dangerous or illegal behavior.
statements.speaker: Jill Grano
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Jill Grano

forum_quotes.question: Boulder voters are being asked to authorize $400 million in new debt through additional property taxes for recreation, public safety and other city facilities as part of ballot issue 2K. Do you support this measure? Why or why not?
forum_quotes.stance_note: Calls for a smaller, more targeted bond; no yes/no in this quote.
forum_quotes.quote: I think we need to go back to the community, get clear on our priorities, and then bring back a smaller, more targeted bond.

forum_quotes.question: What are your feelings about the bus-only lanes and the core arterial network (CAN)? Should Boulder continue prioritizing protected bike lanes?

forum_quotes.question: Do you agree or disagree that our city council is adequately representative of the social, political and economic interests of Boulder? Would you support a study session on proportional representation?
